title: Engineering Advanced Graphene Grids for Imaging of Multi-Component Nanoparticles
content: Graphene is celebrated for its mechanical strength, thermal conductivity, large surface area, and optical transparency, making it indispensable in fields such as optoelectronics, organic transistors, and advanced electronics [1,2]. Mechanical exfoliation (Scotch tape method [3]) was an early approach, but chemical vapor deposition (CVD) soon emerged as a scalable route [4]. By decomposing carbon precursors on copper foils, CVD yields large-area graphene with controlled quality and thickness, highly suitable for next-generation devices requiring reliable performance. Thanks to these remarkable attributes, graphene-based materials have drawn considerable interest for both fundamental research and industrial applications, ranging from flexible electronics to energy storage. Such versatility has spurred ongoing efforts to refine and adapt synthesis for specific use cases.
